fullDescription: A developer documentation platform landing page filed like a library card catalog. The page ground is a warm taupe drawer and every section is a physical manila card laid on it, punched at the bottom edge, inked with a brown border and a hard offset shadow, and headed by a call-number rail. One library-stamp blue is the only colour on the page, the display type is a typewriter face, and the search results and changelog are real ruled ledger tables. Reusable for any docs site, API reference, developer-tools homepage, changelog, knowledge base or archive product.
prompt:
## Resumo
A developer-documentation platform landing page art-directed as a library card catalog. The page ground is a flat warm-taupe drawer #8b7d6f and every content section is a physical manila card #f7f0e4 filed on it: a 1px warm-brown #5a3b28 edge, an 8px hard offset shadow (never a soft blur), a punched rod hole at the bottom centre, and a ruled CALL-NUMBER HEADER RAIL across the top ('№ 004.678 | DOCUMENTATION PLATFORM · SUBJECT CATALOG | FILED 2026') split by vertical divider rules. ONE library-stamp blue #0A48AE is the only chroma anywhere. Display type is Courier Prime 700 at poster scale, stamps and labels are Special Elite uppercase, all UI and body copy is Inter. The nav sits directly on the drawer in warm off-white #FDFCF7. Section by section: (1) the HERO card — a four-line typewriter headline, an Inter subtitle with three keywords bolded inline, then the primary action is a wide DOCUMENTATION SEARCH FIELD with a blue rule and a ⌘K chip, under which four search-result rows run as a real ledger table (Special Elite call number, vertical divider, Inter result title, evenly spaced hairlines); on its right a product-as-proof docs-app screen with its own '№ 200.4 | AUTHENTICATION | REV. 4.2' rail, a sidebar with an active blue-barred row, a tab row, and a 2x2 grid of labelled reference cards. (2) A CIRCULATION RECORD strip card carrying three Courier numerals with Special Elite labels. (3) START HERE — four literal catalog cards, each with an inked call number top-left, a typed uppercase subject heading, ruled writing lines behind the description, and 'OPEN ENTRY →' on a ruled footer; no icon set. (4) READ AN ENTRY — a card holding prose plus a ruled checklist on the left and a near-black #141310 code panel on the right with a cURL/Node/Python tab row and blue-only syntax highlighting. (5) A 'DATE DUE' changelog card — the library due-date slip as a real ruled table: DATE | ENTRY | VERSION header, two vertical dividers, six ruled rows with blue Courier date stamps and outlined version chips. (6) A CIRCULATION · NEW BORROWER CTA card with ruled baselines and a rotated outlined rubber stamp 'INDEXED / 2026' inked onto the manila. (7) A footer on the bare drawer in warm off-white. Everything coloured is the same blue; everything else is taupe, manila, warm off-white or near-black.

## Estilo Visual
Design in an editorial-print card-catalog register. Ground the page in a flat warm taupe #8b7d6f (a drawer, not a paper) and lay every content section on it as a physical manila card #f7f0e4 with a 1px warm-brown #5a3b28 edge, an 8px hard offset shadow (never a soft blur), a punched rod hole at the bottom centre rendered with an inset shadow plus a lower-edge highlight so it reads as a hole with thickness, and a ruled call-number header rail across the top. Confine ALL colour to one library-stamp blue #0A48AE and put it only on meaningful marks: call numbers, column heads, ledger rules, active states, the rubber stamp. Set the display type in Courier Prime 700 at poster scale, stamped micro-type in Special Elite uppercase, and everything else in Inter. Body copy sits on ruled writing lines built from a repeating-linear-gradient. No gradients, no glass, no glow, no dot-grid or line-grid backdrop, no photographs. Pure HTML, CSS and inline SVG.

## Layout e Estrutura

### Drawer, nav and the card system
Fill the page with a flat warm-taupe ground #8b7d6f. Put a thin borderless nav directly on it in warm off-white #FDFCF7: an index-card SVG mark plus a Courier Prime wordmark left, Inter 14px links (Docs, API Reference, Guides, Changelog) centre, and right a hairline-outlined version pill 'v4.2', a 'GitHub 8.4k' text link, and a manila-filled black-bordered button 'Read the docs'. Then define one reusable CARD: manila #f7f0e4, 1px solid rgba(90,59,40,.45) edge, box-shadow 8px 8px 0 rgba(28,22,16,.22), and a 16px punched rod hole at the bottom centre filled with the drawer colour and carrying inset 0 2px 3px rgba(28,22,16,.45) plus inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(253,252,247,.35). Every content section uses that card.

### Call-number header rail
Across the top of each card, run a full-bleed rail bordered top and bottom with a hairline warm-brown rule and split by vertical divider rules into cells of Special Elite 10-11px blue uppercase: a call number ('№ 004.678'), a subject line ('DOCUMENTATION PLATFORM · SUBJECT CATALOG'), and a filing note ('FILED 2026'). Reuse it per section with its own number and subject ('№ 000.0 | CIRCULATION RECORD', '№ 999.0 | CIRCULATION · NEW BORROWER').

### Hero card
Inside the first card, left-weighted at ~55%: a four-line Courier Prime 700 headline at ~62px with tight leading ('Every endpoint, filed where your team will actually find it.'); an Inter subtitle with exactly three keywords bolded inline; then the hero's primary action, a wide manila search field with a 1px blue border, a hard 3px blue offset shadow, a magnifier, the placeholder 'Search 1,284 pages of documentation' and a Special Elite ⌘K chip at its right end. Directly beneath it, four search-result rows as a real ledger: a Special Elite call number in a fixed-width left column, a vertical divider rule, an Inter result title, and an evenly spaced hairline under each row. No glow, no gradient band, no background grid.

### Product-as-proof docs screen
On the hero card's right, float the product as an abstract docs-app SCREEN (never a literal screenshot, and never punched — a screen is not a card): a white panel with a 1px blue border and its own '№ 200.4 | AUTHENTICATION | REV. 4.2' rail, a left sidebar with Special Elite group labels and one active row marked by a solid blue left bar and a tinted fill, a tab row with a blue-underlined active tab, an H2 plus one real sentence of body copy, a hairline rule, and a 2x2 grid of pale-blue reference cards each carrying a thin blue line icon, a real title and a three-word description. Generic labels only, and no placeholder grey bars.

### Catalog cards
For the START HERE row, build four literal catalog cards rather than feature tiles: inked Special Elite call number top-left, a hairline rule, a typed uppercase Courier Prime subject heading, a description sitting on ruled writing lines (a repeating-linear-gradient of blue hairlines every 28px, with the text line-height matched to the rule spacing), and 'OPEN ENTRY →' in Special Elite on a ruled footer. No icon set: the call number and the ruled lines are the ornament. Leave clear space at the bottom for the punch.

### Code panel and DATE DUE changelog
In the entry card, pair left-hand prose plus a ruled checklist with a near-black #141310 code panel on the right: a Special Elite route label, a cURL/Node/Python tab row with the active tab underlined, a copy chip, and ~18 lines of Courier request-and-response code whose ONLY syntax colour is the same blue plus warm off-white and grey. Then build the changelog as a 'DATE DUE' card: a centred underlined Courier title, a DATE | ENTRY | VERSION header row on a faint blue fill bounded by 2px blue rules, two vertical divider rules running the full table, and six evenly spaced ruled rows each carrying a blue Courier date stamp, an Inter release title and a small outlined version chip.

### CTA card and footer
Close with a circulation card, not a dark banner: an oversized manila card with a '№ 999.0 | CIRCULATION · NEW BORROWER' rail, a Courier Prime headline, one line of body copy on ruled writing lines, a solid near-black primary button and an outlined secondary button sitting at the right on desktop, and a rotated outlined rubber stamp 'INDEXED / 2026' in Special Elite inked onto the manila at real contrast near the bottom edge. Then a footer directly on the bare drawer in warm off-white: wordmark, four short link columns, a hairline rule above, and a Special Elite line 'PROPERTY OF THE ENGINEERING LIBRARY'.

## Componentes Especiais de UI

### Filed-card section system — The page's sectioning IS the concept: every section is a physical card on a drawer.
Define one card primitive and use it for every content section: manila #f7f0e4 on a warm-taupe #8b7d6f ground, a 1px warm-brown edge, a hard 8px offset shadow with zero blur, and a punched rod hole at the bottom centre. Because the sections themselves are the cards, the concept cannot be stripped off the page as decoration — remove the ornament and the layout still reads as a drawer of filed cards.

### Call-number header rail — A metadata rail that heads every card with a call number, subject and filing note.
Head each card with a full-bleed rail bounded by hairline rules and split by vertical dividers into Special Elite 10-11px uppercase cells in the accent colour: a Dewey-style call number, a subject line, and a filing note. It gives every section an identity, a filing logic and a place for micro-metadata that would otherwise become a decorative pill row.

### Punched rod hole with real thickness — The library-card punch, rendered so it reads as a hole rather than a dot.
Place a 16px circle at the bottom centre of each card, filled with the page ground colour and carrying inset 0 2px 3px rgba(28,22,16,.45) plus inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(253,252,247,.35) inside a hairline warm-brown border, so it reads as punched through the stock with real thickness. Never put it on a panel that represents a product screen — a screen is not a card, and the mismatch makes the hero ambiguous.

### Ruled ledger table (search results and changelog) — The due-date table used twice: once as live search results, once as the changelog.
Build a real ledger: a header row over a faint accent fill bounded by 2px accent rules, one or two full-height vertical column dividers, and evenly spaced horizontal hairlines under each row. Use it for the hero's search-result rows (call number | result title) and again for the changelog (date | entry | version), so the same material device carries two different jobs on the same page.

### Ruled writing lines behind body copy — Body text sitting on catalog-card rules rather than on blank stock.
Give body copy a repeating-linear-gradient of accent hairlines every 28px and set the text line-height to 28px so the words sit ON the rules. It is a one-line CSS device that turns any paragraph into a filled-in card and is the cheapest way to make a print conceit structural rather than decorative.

### Search-first documentation hero — The hero's primary action is the docs search field, not a pair of buttons.
Make the hero's primary action a wide search field with a hairline accent border, a hard offset shadow, a magnifier and a ⌘K chip, and put four real result rows directly beneath it in the ledger style. For a documentation product this is the honest hierarchy — the thing a visitor actually wants to do is search — and it doubles as proof the index exists.

### Single-accent stamp-ink system — One library-stamp blue carries every coloured mark on the page.
Confine ALL colour to one library-stamp blue #0A48AE and spend it only on meaningful marks: call numbers, column heads, ledger rules, the active sidebar row, the active tab underline, code syntax, version chips and the rubber stamp. Everything else stays taupe, manila, warm off-white or near-black. The single ink is what keeps a heavily-materialised page from reading as costume.

style.description: Editorial print materiality applied to a developer-tools product page: a filed-card system, not a paper texture. The register is a mid-tone warm-taupe drawer #8b7d6f carrying manila cards #f7f0e4, warm-brown inked edges #5a3b28, near-black type #141310, warm off-white chrome #FDFCF7, and ONE library-stamp blue #0A48AE as the only chroma. Type does the character work: Courier Prime 700 as the display face at poster scale (a typewriter, deliberately not the sans every dev-tools site defaults to), Special Elite for stamped micro-type (call numbers, column heads, rubber stamps), Inter for all UI and body. The material vocabulary is strictly physical and CSS-only: hard offset shadows never soft blurs, hairline ruled ledger lines, a punched rod hole with an inset shadow and a lower-edge highlight, and repeating-linear-gradient writing lines behind body copy. No gradient, no glass, no glow, no dot-grid or line-grid backdrop, no photography, no icon-set decoration on the catalog cards. The value structure is the point: mid-tone ground, light cards, one near-black panel, so the load-bearing content always sits clearly above its surface.

layout_and_structure.description: A full scrolling landing where the sectioning system IS the concept: nav on the bare drawer, then a stack of filed cards — hero card, circulation-record strip card, four loose catalog cards, an entry card holding a code panel, a DATE DUE changelog card, a circulation CTA card — then a footer back on the bare drawer. Each card carries a call-number header rail, a bottom punch and a hard offset shadow. Fully fluid: the hero splits 55/45 on desktop and stacks on mobile, the catalog cards run 4-up then 2-up then 1-up, the docs-app mock simplifies on mobile (its optional tab is dropped and its 2x2 card grid becomes one column) rather than scaling down.
